answers.solution:
I diagnosed and verified the fix. Note: the original trouble repo was not present in the sandbox, so I reconstructed the `internal/sensors` package from the problem statement, reproduced the exact red, applied the fix, and falsified it.

## Root cause

`RuleDirFingerprint` hashed only `path + size + mtime`:

```go
fmt.Fprintf(h, "%s\x00%d\x00%d\n", name, info.Size(), info.ModTime().UnixNano())
```

A same-size content rewrite with a pinned/unchanged mtime (coarse fs granularity, `tar -x`, `rsync -t`, `os.Chtimes`) leaves *every* stat field identical → fingerprint unchanged → the 60s sweep misses the real change and never reloads. The test asserted "the mtime moved", i.e. it asserted a property of the **filesystem**, not the code.

## Fix

Fold a streamed SHA-256 content digest into the fingerprint alongside metadata, using `io.Copy(h, f)` so bytes are never buffered:

```go
fmt.Fprintf(h, "%s\x00%d\x00%d\x00", name, info.Size(), info.ModTime().UnixNano())
f, err := os.Open(path)
if err != nil { return "", err }
_, copyErr := io.Copy(h, f)
closeErr := f.Close()
// ... surface both errors
h.Write([]byte("\n"))
```

Metadata stays in the digest (path binding); nothing-changed stays stable so the sweep doesn't reload every tick.

## Test

`TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange` now asserts the hostile condition directly — same-length rewrite + `os.Chtimes` pins mtime equal — plus a natural polled edit/removal half with a 3s deadline (> 1s granularity) and a stability check.

## Verification results

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Pre-fix `go test` | **FAIL** — `pinned-mtime content change did not trigger reload` / `the mtime fingerprint did not change after an edit` |
| Post-fix `go test -run TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange -v` | PASS |
| `go test ./internal/sensors/ -count=10` | ok |
| `go test -race ./internal/sensors/ -count=3` | ok |
| `go vet` / `gofmt -l` | clean |
| Falsification: buggy `rules.go` restored in `/tmp/falsify` | **FAIL** again |

The full self-contained write-up (root cause, complete `rules.go`, complete `reload_test.go`, exact commands, expected-outcome table) is at:

- **`/home/kara/SOLUTION.md`**
- Reproduction module: `/home/kara/trouble` (`internal/sensors/rules.go`, `internal/sensors/reload_test.go`)
- Falsified copy: `/tmp/falsify`

signatures.description: Go test asserts a file-mtime-derived fingerprint changes after a same-size rewrite, but the fingerprint hashed path+size+mtime only, so on a coarse-granularity filesystem (or a tar-synced/restored tree) the mtime does not move inside the test window and the assertion is a deterministic false red on clean machines while green on the ns-granularity dev box. Product-side the same blindness makes a 60s mtime-sweep backstop MISS a real content change.
